title: Sofacy_Fysbis_Backdoor_Investigation_6d5
description: Investigate and respond to a Sofacy group compromise using the Fysbis backdoor in a target network.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The target network has been compromised by the Sofacy group using the Fysbis backdoor. Your task is to investigate and respond to this incident. The Fysbis backdoor is a modular Linux trojan/backdoor that implements plug-in and controller modules as distinct classes. It includes both 32-bit and 64-bit versions of ELF binaries and can install itself with or without root privileges.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: Access the target host `target` (IP: 192.168.50.5) in the cloud sandbox.
levels.local_content: Access the target host `target` (IP: 192.168.50.5) in the local sandbox. Username: `cyrano`, Password: `cyrano`.

levels.title: Identify Suspicious Service
levels.content: Identify and investigate an unauthorized or suspicious service running on the target host. Enumerate running services and distinguish legitimate from suspicious services. The flag is the name of the suspicious service.
levels.solution: Check the systemd services and look for any unusual or unauthorized services. The service name `systemkernelservicedefender.service` should be identified as the suspicious service flag.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Systemd services can be listed using specific commands. Start by enumerating all running services.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl list-units --type=service` to list all running services.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: Look for a service named `systemkernelservicedefender.service` in the list of running services.

levels.title: Determine Persistence Mechanism
levels.content: Determine how the suspicious service is automatically started after reboot. Identify persistence mechanisms (e.g., systemd, cron, scheduled task). The flag is the name of the persistence mechanism.
levels.solution: Investigate the systemd service configuration and timers. The persistence mechanism should be identified as a systemd timer `lab-checkin.timer` flag.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Persistence mechanisms can be identified by examining systemd timers and other scheduled tasks.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl list-timers` to list all systemd timers.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: Look for a timer named `lab-checkin.timer` in the list of systemd timers.

levels.title: Locate Malicious Artifact
levels.content: Locate the executable or file associated with the suspicious activity. Correlate processes with files on disk and identify malicious artifacts. The flag is the path to the malicious artifact.
levels.solution: Check the scripts and executables associated with the suspicious service. The filename `/usr/local/bin/lab-checkin.sh` should be identified as the malicious artifact flag.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Malicious artifacts can often be found in directories like `/usr/local/bin/` or `/tmp/`.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Use the command `ls -la /usr/local/bin/` to list files in the `/usr/local/bin/` directory.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: Look for a file named `lab-checkin.sh` in the `/usr/local/bin/` directory.
